text:
claude-multi-desktop

 Run multiple Claude Desktop accounts at the same time on one Mac. Each window has its own sign-in, and all of them share one Claude Code setup, so a session in one account can send work to a session in another. 

One bash script · no dependencies · never modifies Claude.app · macOS

 Unofficial, for legitimate use only. It is built for one person with a personal and a work Claude account (see who it is for). Do not use it to get around usage limits or to share accounts; using several accounts to abuse usage quotas is not supported. See the disclaimer.

Website · Who it is for · Quick start · Install · Icons and names · Sessions talk across accounts · What is shared · FAQ · Changelog

 
 
 

 

 What makes it different

Claude Desktop runs one account at a time. If you open it again, the same window comes back to the front. Other tools work around this by keeping every account fully separate, Claude Code setup included. This tool keeps the sign-ins separate and lets the accounts share the rest, and that has three uses:

1. Separate accounts, one setup. Each window signs in to its own Claude account and keeps its own chats, projects and plan. Claude Code in every window reads the same /.claude : your skills, CLAUDE.md , memory, MCP servers, hooks and settings. If you write a skill once, every account loads it the next time it starts a session, and you never copy setup files between accounts.

2. Sessions talk across accounts. Every account records its running Claude Code sessions in the same place, so a session in your Work window can see the sessions in your Personal window and send one a message, using Claude Code's built-in ListAgents and SendMessage tools. You can type "ask the trip planning session in my Personal account to check the hotel list" and the message reaches that session with no copy and paste. claude-multi-desktop peers shows which session runs in which account:

 

3. No dependencies, nothing patched. It is one bash script you can read in five minutes. Each launcher is a small app that opens the Claude.app you already have with Electron's public --user-data-dir flag. It makes no copy of Claude.app, re-signs nothing and runs nothing in the background. When Claude updates, every account gets the update, and uninstalling means deleting the launcher.

 Who it is for

claude-multi-desktop was designed for one person who has two Claude accounts of their own, a personal one and a work one, that cannot be opened in the same window. That happens in two cases:

- Your personal and work accounts use different email addresses. Each email is its own sign-in, and Claude Desktop holds one sign-in at a time, so without this tool you sign out of one account to use the other.
- Your work account came before your personal one. For example, your employer set up a seat under your work email before you had a personal account, and the personal account you added later is a separate sign-in.

In both cases the tool gives each account its own window, so both stay signed in, while Claude Code keeps one setup for you as a single user.

 Other uses. The launchers work for any account folder, so the tool can technically run other kinds of profiles too. That is not what it was built for. If you use it outside the two cases above, you do so at your own risk, and the authors accept no responsibility for the consequences.

 Usage quotas. Running several accounts to farm, pool or stretch usage limits is not supported. Issues and pull requests that ask for help with that will be closed.

 Quick start

You need macOS and Claude Desktop in /Applications .

 

That's it. You now have Claude Work and Claude Main in /Applications , so Spotlight, Launchpad and the Dock all find them. Drag them to the Dock and click whichever account you want; both can stay open side by side.

No Homebrew, or would you rather not use Terminal? Install lists a Mac installer, a disk image with a double-click app, npm, PyPI and a Claude Code plugin.

 Install

Homebrew is the shortest way. The others are for people without Homebrew, or who would rather not use Terminal.

 Homebrew

 

 Mac installer (.pkg)

Download the .pkg file from the latest release and open it. It installs the claude-multi-desktop command to /usr/local/bin and the double-click app Claude Multi Desktop to /Applications .

The installer is not signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks it the first time you open it: see If macOS blocks the app or installer.

To uninstall it:

 

 Disk image (.dmg)

Download the .dmg file from the same release page, drag Claude Multi Desktop to Applications and double-click it. It asks for an account name, an icon style (a coloured letter, your Claude icon with a letter badge, or a picture) and a colour, then makes the launcher and opens it. It can also open, rename or remove launchers you already made. You never need Terminal.

The app is not signed with an Apple Developer ID either: see If macOS blocks the app or installer. The disk image carries the same steps as a text file next to the app.

 If macOS blocks the app or installer

If macOS says "Apple could not verify 'Claude Multi Desktop' is free of malware" : the app and the installer are not signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time you open them. The code is open source, and you only need to allow it once.

 macOS 15 (Sequoia) and later 

1. Double-click the app (or the .pkg ) once. When macOS blocks it, click Done .
2. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and scroll down to the Security section. You will see "'Claude Multi Desktop' was blocked to protect your Mac." (for the installer, its file name). Click Open Anyway .
3. Enter your Mac login password (or use Touch ID). If macOS asks once more, click Open Anyway again. From then on it opens normally.

 macOS 14 (Sonoma) and earlier 

1. Right-click (or Control-click) the app (or the .pkg ) and choose Open .
2. Click Open in the dialog. You only do this once.

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
You need macOS and Claude Desktop in /Applications.

brew install jackson-cmd/tap/claude-multi-desktop
claude-multi-desktop add Work            # a launcher called "Claude Work" with its own sign-in
claude-multi-desktop open Work           # opens a second Claude window; sign in with your other account
claude-multi-desktop add Main --default  # a launcher for the account you already use

That's it. You now have Claude Work and Claude Main in ~/Applications, so Spotlight, Launchpad and the Dock all find them. Drag them to the Dock and click whichever account you want; both can stay open side by side.

No Homebrew, or would you rather not use Terminal? Install lists a Mac installer, a disk image with a double-click app, npm, PyPI and a Claude Code plugin.

usage.title: Commands
usage.html:
Command What it does
add NAME Make the launcher Claude NAME with its own sign-in (folder Claude-NAME)
add NAME --default Make a launcher for the account you already use
add NAME --color HEX Choose the icon colour, e.g. --color 7A5AE0
add NAME --icon claude Use your own Claude icon with a coloured letter badge, drawn on your Mac
add NAME --icon /path/to/picture Use any PNG, JPEG, HEIC or ICNS picture as the icon
icon NAME --icon … --color HEX Change the icon or colour of an existing launcher
rename NAME NEW Rename a launcher and keep its sign-in and chats (the account folder keeps its name)
list Show your launchers, their folders and which ones are open
list --names Print the launcher names only, one per line
open NAME Open that account's window
peers Show the Claude Code sessions running in every account
remove NAME Delete the launcher and keep the account's sign-in and chats
remove NAME --delete-data Also delete that account's folder (asks you to type the name; never touches your first account)

Launchers go to ~/Applications; set CMD_APPS_DIR to put them elsewhere. If Claude.app is not in /Applications or ~/Applications, set CLAUDE_APP=/path/to/Claude.app.
